drafts.title: fix(compiler-core): resolve dotted component tags from props in script setup
drafts.description: In a `
drafts.summary:
ROOT CAUSE: packages/compiler-core/src/transforms/transformElement.ts. The dotted-tag branch of `resolveComponentType` (lines 318-324) calls `resolveSetupReference` for the namespace. `resolveSetupReference` (lines 347-388) checks only the SETUP_* and LITERAL_CONST binding types, so it returns undefined for BindingTypes.PROPS. The tag then falls through to `resolveComponent('info.icon')` in step 5. That call finds no component, so the runtime treats the tag as a native element. This explains the reproduction: `abc` is a setup binding and `props` is a setup binding, so `<abc.icon>` and `<props.info.icon>` render, but `info` is a prop and `<info.icon>` does not.

This trace comes from code reading and from the decoded reproduction. The failure was not run.

DECISIONS:
1. In the dotted-tag branch only, when the namespace has the binding type PROPS, return the props access expression plus the remaining part of the tag.
2. Generate `$props.info.icon` in non-inline mode. `$props` is a render function argument (codegen.ts:233).
3. Generate `__props.info.icon` in inline mode. Reuse `genPropsAccessExp`, which transformExpression.ts:198 uses for the same binding type.
4. Keep the guard that skips this resolution when `bindingMetadata` is absent or `__isScriptSetup` is false.

REJECTED:
- Add the PROPS check inside `resolveSetupReference`. That function also serves bare tags (line 314) and custom directives (line 901). With that change, a prop `myComp` would capture `<my-comp>` and hide a globally registered component, and a prop `vFoo` would capture `v-foo`. The issue does not ask for this behavior change.
- Tell users to write `<props.info.icon>` or `<component :is>`. That is a workaround and it leaves the root cause.
- Support PROPS_ALIASED (destructured props). The issue does not ask for this support.

NOTE: The checkout has a detached HEAD at fc772db and no local `main` ref. docs/arch and .karst/worktrees do not exist, so no arch key applies and no in-flight work overlaps.
constraints: Test: with `info` bound as BindingTypes.PROPS, non-inline `<info.icon/>` must generate tag `$props.info.icon` and must not call resolveComponent.
Test: with `info` bound as BindingTypes.PROPS and inline: true, `<info.icon/>` must generate tag `__props.info.icon` and must not call resolveComponent.
Put the tests next to 'resolve namespaced component from setup bindings' in compiler-core transformElement.spec.ts.

notDone.item: Add the PROPS binding check inside `resolveSetupReference`, so it returns `unref(__props["name"])` in inline mode and `unref($props["name"])` in non-inline mode. The drafts reject this change on purpose. They only patch the dotted-tag branch.

Wrap the props access in the `unref` helper (`context.helperString(UNREF)`) and use bracket-string access (`__props["info"]`, `$props["info"]`). The drafts generate plain `$props.info.icon` and `__props.info.icon` with no `unref`, so the generated tag string differs from the one the tests expect.

resolve namespaced component from props bindings (inline)

drafts.title: [Select] Forward disabled to the hidden input element
drafts.description:
Root cause: packages/material-ui/src/Select/SelectInput.js takes `disabled` out of props by destructuring. The file applies `disabled` to the display div, as aria-disabled and classes, and to the icon. The file does not apply `disabled` to the `<input>`, and `...other` no longer contains the prop. Thus `<TextField select disabled />` renders an enabled input, and a form submit includes the value.

Work:
1. In SelectInput.js, add `disabled={disabled}` to the `<input>` element.
2. In packages/material-ui/src/Select/Select.test.js, add the test that the constraints describe.
drafts.summary:
Decisions: Make the one-prop fix in SelectInput.js. InputBase already passes `fcs.disabled` to the input component, so a disabled FormControl and TextField reach SelectInput through the same path. No change is necessary in InputBase, Select, or TextField. Keep aria-disabled on the display div, because the issue does not ask to remove it.

Rejected: A change in TextField, because the defect is in SelectInput and a bare `<Select disabled />` has the same defect. Removal of the input `name` when disabled, because it is a workaround and does not give the input the disabled attribute.

Findings: The repository has no docs/arch directory, so no @arch key applies. `draft list` was empty and no ticket worktree exists. The local `main` ref does not exist, so the history check used HEAD.
constraints: Test: `<Select disabled value="" />` renders an `input` element with the `disabled` attribute.
Test: `<Select disabled={false} value="" />` renders an `input` element without the `disabled` attribute.

f2pCoverage.test: /home/material-ui/packages/material-ui/src/Select/Select.test.js:<Select /> accessibility sets disabled attribute in input when component is disabled

drafts.title: [system] Apply style() transform when the theme value is a function or an array
drafts.description:
Root cause: in packages/material-ui-system/src/style.js, getValue() calls transform only in the final else branch (plain object theme value). When the theme value at themeKey is a function or an array, getValue() returns without a call to transform. The issue example uses themeKey 'spacing', and theme.spacing is such a value, so the transform never runs.

Fix: in getValue() in packages/material-ui-system/src/style.js, move the `if (transform)` block out of the else branch, so that it runs after all three branches. Add the regression test in packages/material-ui-system/src/style.test.js.
drafts.summary:
Decisions:
- Fix the root cause in getValue(). This is the same change that the issue requests from stale PR #16439.
- The transform receives the value that the theme lookup resolved. If the lookup finds no array entry, the transform receives the user value.
- Change only style.js and style.test.js.

Rejected:
- A wrapper or a special case for themeKey 'spacing': this is a workaround, and the defect applies to all function and array theme values.
- A change to spacing.js or to the docs: the issue does not ask for it.

Known effect:
- A built-in `border` style with a function or array theme.borders now has its numeric result changed by getBorder to `${value}px solid`. String results do not change, so the existing 'should transform the prop correctly' test (output3) must continue to pass without an edit.
- Styles without a themeKey (for example `width`) use the object branch, so they do not change.

Not verified in this session: the tests were not run, and the codesandbox from the issue was not opened. The root cause comes from a read of the code.

Note: the checkout is a detached HEAD at 3506dda, and the ref 'main' does not resolve locally. The repository has no docs/arch directory, so no @arch keys apply. `draft list` showed no other drafts, and there are no open ticket worktrees.
constraints: Test must check: with a function theme value at themeKey, transform runs on the function result and the output has the transformed value.
Test must check: with an array theme value at themeKey, transform runs on the array entry and the output has the transformed value.
Test must check: with an array theme value and a missing index, transform runs on the user value.
Test must fail before the fix: the transform output is absent from the style result.
